title: Optimal one-shot quantum multiple-access one-time-pad rate region
summary: Determine the exact one-shot reliable-and-private rate region for the quantum multiple-access one-time pad.

formal_statement.body: For one copy of an admissible shared state in the source's quantum multiple-access one-time-pad task and fixed reliability and secrecy tolerances $(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec}})$, characterize exactly the achievable message-size region for all senders. Prove matching achievability and converse bounds that allow joint decoding and state the dependence on both error tolerances; successive decoding and time sharing alone need not attain the optimum.

assumptions: The senders, receiver, eavesdropper, and local-encoding task are those of the source
Reliability is bounded by a fixed decoding-error tolerance
Secrecy is bounded by a fixed trace-distance tolerance
The optimal region may require joint decoding rather than only successive decoding and time sharing
scope.unresolved_remainder: Cheng, Liu, and Xi give a published achievable inner bound using position-based coding, joint typicality, and convex split. No matching converse or proof that this inner bound is the exact optimal one-shot region was found.

progress.summary: The source identifies determination of the optimal one-shot QMA-OTP region as a future direction requiring more than successive decoding and time sharing.
Cheng, Liu, and Xi publish a one-shot achievable inner bound, but do not provide the matching converse needed for the optimal region.
